news.title: Inside Arsenal star Riccardo Calafiori's incredible summer backpacking trip to get over World Cup heartbreak
news.lede: RICCARDO CALAFIORI went backpacking this summer to get over the pain of missing out on the World Cup. Italy failed to qualify for football’s biggest party for the third tournament in a row and the Arsenal defender couldn’t bear to watch. Instead, he and his friends went travelling around South America, taking in the sights of Argentina, Rio de Janeiro and the waterfalls of the Iguazu River. It was exactly the sort of holiday you would expect from Calafiori, who plays football with a youthful joy and freedom.

news.title: World champion and the Paris enigma to the fore: have France Football's criteria become mere ink on paper?
news.lede: Every year, French magazine "France Football" reveals its list of Ballon d'Or nominees. And as has become the norm in recent seasons, controversy erupts the moment the names go public. Followers always question the transparency of football's most prestigious individual award, and just how faithfully the stated criteria are applied when the nominees are chosen. France Football have tried to update the regulations and lend the process a fair, objective feel.

news.title: Ballon d’Or Goalkeeper of the Year: All nominees
news.lede: And this year, it brings a new set of nominees with results influenced by not just club football, but also the FIFA World Cup 2026. The Yashin Trophy, named after the goalkeeping legend Lev Yashin, will be awarded to one goalkeeper each in the men’s and women’s categories. news.title: Spain Dismisses Ceuta Crisis Impact on 2030 World Cup Final Debate
news.lede: Rabat – Spain’s Minister for Education, Vocational Training and Sport, Milagros Tolón, has rejected suggestions that the migration crisis in Ceuta could affect the decision over the venue of the 2030 FIFA World Cup final. Speaking to Spanish public broadcaster TVE, Tolón said she does not believe the situation in Ceuta will influence FIFA’s decision on where to stage the tournament’s showpiece match. “Who decides is FIFA,” Tolón said, stressing that the Spanish Ministry of Sport is working with all parties involved in the 2030 World Cup to deliver what she described as the best edition of the tournament. She also pointed to Spain’s football success and sporting infrastructure as reasons for her confidence in the country’s chances.
